1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

- **GPR39 and 15-HETE identified as core drivers of coronary autoregulation** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2025.12.23.696315)
  - Metabolomic profiling in canine coronary stenosis models demonstrated that 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (15-HETE) levels linearly correlate with coronary driving pressure (CDP; r² = 0.47, p = 0.0024).
  - Administration of the selective GPR39 antagonist VC108 reduced coronary microvascular resistance (p = 0.01) and completely abolished coronary autoregulation, making blood flow pressure-dependent (r² = 0.96, p = 0.004).

- **Ex vivo directed evolution of gut microbiome extends lifespan in Drosophila** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.04.742805)
  - Ex vivo directed evolution generated a paraquat-resistant *Lactiplantibacillus plantarum* strain that, upon re-colonization, reduced age-related gut pathology and extended host lifespan.
  - Longevity benefits were linked to increased bacterial acetate production, and direct dietary acetate administration was sufficient to recapitulate lifespan extension.

- **Pulsed transcranial photobiomodulation alters EEG oscillations in parameter-dependent manner** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.26.656199)
  - A 46-participant 256-channel EEG trial evaluated near-infrared light delivery to the right forehead across varying wavelengths, pulsation frequencies, and irradiances.
  - Wavelength dictated response character (808 nm drove broad posterior suppression; 1064 nm selectively increased frontal gamma), while 10 Hz pulsation induced greater gamma enhancement than 40 Hz, contrasting with neural entrainment predictions.
  - Biological analysis identified sex as a primary moderator of electrophysiological response, whereas skin tone and irradiance had no significant effect.

- **BBB-penetrating small molecule stabilizes transthyretin for Alzheimer's disease** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42571862/)
  - Preclinical study evaluated a novel blood-brain barrier-penetrating small molecule designed to stabilize transthyretin tetramers as a potential therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease.

- **Uric acid-to-HDL ratio predicts chronic kidney disease risk in MASLD** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572097/)
  - Prospective cohort and multi-omics study identified the uric acid-to-HDL ratio as a predictive biomarker for incident chronic kidney disease risk across lean and non-lean MASLD populations.

- **In vitro cytotoxic activity of platinum-Mesalazine complex in colorectal cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42571672/)
  - Preclinical study demonstrated enhanced anticancer activity of a platinum-Mesalazine complex against colorectal cancer cell lines via apoptotic modulation and non-intercalative DNA binding.

- **Atlas integrates CAR-based immunotherapy target profiles in lung cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42571830/)
  - Multi-database integration synthesized current data on CAR-based immunotherapies and target landscapes in lung cancer R&D.

- **Review outlines utility and limitations of urinary biomarkers in heart failure** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572043/)
  - Review details the clinical application, risk stratification value, and diagnostic limitations of urinary biomarkers in heart failure management.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

- **[Biotech]** **Phase 2 trial evaluates PARP inhibitor TSL-1502 in BRCA-mutated breast cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572030/)
  - Randomized Phase 2 study evaluated the PARP inhibitor TSL-1502 in patients with germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

- **Randomized trial evaluates high-frequency rTMS in adolescent gaming disorder** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42572071/)
  - A 4-week randomized controlled trial with a 24-week follow-up evaluated high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for craving reduction in adolescents.

- **AI echo INSIGHT trial tests artificial intelligence in echocardiogram interpretation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42571809/)
  - Prospective, blinded randomized trial investigated artificial intelligence performance and diagnostic utility in interpreting echocardiograms.

5. **Business & Strategy**

- **[Big Pharma]** **Sanofi experiences shortages of Pompe disease treatments Myozyme and Nexviazyme** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/08/09/sanofi-pompe-disease-drug-shortage-myozyme-nexviazyme/)
  - Sanofi is facing supply shortages for two key enzyme replacement therapies for Pompe disease, Myozyme and Nexviazyme.
  - Inventory constraints have drawn concern from patient advocacy groups regarding supply stability and treatment continuity.

**Worth watching:** The identification of GPR39 and 15-HETE as core orchestrators of coronary autoregulation offers an unexplored mechanism for therapeutic modulation of coronary microvascular resistance and ischemic cardiovascular disease.

- Biology & Health
    - [403 ‒ Peptides: separating scientific promise from marketing hype](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Km_01CLEkYU) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Establishes a five-question evaluation framework and a three-tier evidence classification system to analyze peptides individually based on biological mechanism, clinical efficacy, and safety profile.
        - Evaluates specific compounds such as BPC-157 (noting unclear mechanisms, lack of human clinical trials, and unknown risks) and CJC-1295 (distinguishing mere biological activity from meaningful clinical benefit).
        - Warns that user testimonials, doctor prescriptions, compounding pharmacy access, and third-party testing do not validate unapproved peptides, stressing the necessity of placebo-controlled trials and FDA approval.
        - Highlights the risks of gray-market products, noting that scientific evidence for FDA-approved peptides cannot be extrapolated to unvalidated gray-market versions.
        - Asserts that peptide claims must be falsifiable and backed by rigorous scientific evidence before being adopted for widespread clinical or wellness use.
